title: Letters to a Young Poet
note: Go into yourself. The whole book is that sentence, patiently unfolded.

title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
note: The wave holds still and the mountain moves — I kept switching which one I believed.

title: Nocturne No. 20 in C-sharp minor
note: Heard in a small hall, almost by accident. The quietest music I know that still argues.

title: Wings of Desire
note: Angels who envy us the taste of coffee. A film about attention itself.

title: In the light of what we know
note: That a commonplace book is not a diary: it records what struck you, not what happened to you. The difference is the whole project.

title: The Cherry Orchard
note: Everyone talks past everyone, beautifully. The axe in the last act lands on the audience.

title: To the Lighthouse
note: Time passes in ten pages and takes a war with it.

title: Ozymandias
verse:
I met a traveller from an antique land,
Who said—"Two vast and trunkless legs of stone
Stand in the desert. . . . Near them, on the sand,
Half sunk a shattered visage lies, whose frown,
And wrinkled lip, and sneer of cold command,
Tell that its sculptor well those passions read
Which yet survive, stamped on these lifeless things,
The hand that mocked them, and the heart that fed;
And on the pedestal, these words appear:
My name is Ozymandias, King of Kings;
Look on my Works, ye Mighty, and despair!
Nothing beside remains. Round the decay
Of that colossal Wreck, boundless and bare
The lone and level sands stretch far away."

title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
note: She is mid-turn. Vermeer painted the half-second before a word.

title: Symphony No. 5
note: The Adagietto, live, is a different instrument than any recording of it.

title: We live as we dream — alone
note: Conrad, Heart of Darkness. Copied out on the train home.

title: Vermeer retrospective
note: Twenty-eight rooms of stillness. Left with a taste for smaller paintings.

title: The Death of Ivan Ilyich
note: The most frightening book I know that contains no monster.

title: Pale Blue Dot
note: Sagan's point is not that we are small. It is that everyone you have ever loved lived on the same pixel.
